categories.main_business_segments: Parsons operates in two primary business segments: Federal Solutions and Critical Infrastructure. Federal Solutions (59% of 2024 revenue) delivers advanced technology, engineering, and mission-critical services to U.S. government agencies, including defense, intelligence, and civil sectors. Critical Infrastructure (41% of 2024 revenue) provides program management, engineering, and digital solutions for complex physical and digital infrastructure projects globally, serving both public and private sector clients.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Parsons leverages advanced technologies such as artificial intelligence/machine learning, cyber and electronic warfare, digital engineering (including digital twins and model-based systems engineering), advanced analytics, and systems integration. The company develops both software and hardware products, provides systems integration, and employs agile, collaborative development and rapid prototyping methods to deliver mission-specific solutions for defense, intelligence, and infrastructure clients.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Key customers include U.S. federal government agencies (Department of Defense, Intelligence Community, NASA, Department of Energy, Homeland Security, etc.), state and local governments, international public sector clients (notably in the Middle East), and private sector infrastructure owners. Major end markets are national security (defense, intelligence, cyber, space), transportation (aviation, rail, highways), environmental remediation, water/wastewater, and urban development.
categories.geographic_coverage: Parsons has a global footprint, with significant operations in North America (U.S. and Canada), Europe, the Middle East (notably Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar), and Africa. The company maintains offices and project sites in 38 U.S. states and 15 countries, with a strong presence in the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) region and major U.S. metropolitan areas.
categories.supply_chain_position: Parsons primarily operates as a systems integrator and solutions provider, positioned downstream in the supply chain. The company delivers end-to-end services, from concept and design through implementation, integration, and ongoing support, often acting as a prime contractor or program manager for large-scale government and infrastructure projects.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include expanding in high-growth markets such as cyber and intelligence, space and missile defense, critical infrastructure protection, transportation, environmental remediation, and urban development. R&D and innovation are focused on artificial intelligence, digital transformation, cyber/electronic warfare, space systems, PFAS remediation, and smart infrastructure. The company pursues technology-driven acquisitions to enhance capabilities and move up the value chain as a solutions integrator and software provider.
categories.revenue_model: Parsons generates revenue primarily through long-term contracts for services, including cost-plus, time-and-materials, and fixed-price contracts. Revenue streams include engineering and consulting services, program management, systems integration, software and hardware product sales, and recurring digital solutions. The company also earns incentive and award fees based on performance criteria in government contracts.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: In Federal Solutions, Parsons competes with major U.S. federal systems integrators such as Booz Allen Hamilton, CACI, Leidos, and SAIC. In Critical Infrastructure, key competitors include AECOM, Jacobs, Stantec, Tetra Tech, and WSP. Parsons is positioned as a technology-driven, agile integrator with a strong reputation for innovation, high win rates, and long-term customer relationships, often competing for technically complex, mission-critical assignments.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2024, Parsons reported $6.8 billion in revenue, $235 million in net income, and $605 million in Adjusted EBITDA, with a 24% year-over-year revenue growth. The company has a backlog of $8.9 billion and maintains strong win rates (72% overall, 84% re-compete in 2024). Federal Solutions grew 33% and Critical Infrastructure 13% year-over-year, reflecting robust organic and acquisition-driven growth.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Parsons differentiates itself through its integrated, technology-driven solutions that address complex, evolving challenges in national security and critical infrastructure. The company emphasizes its ability to deliver innovative, agile, and scalable offerings, leveraging deep domain expertise, advanced technologies, and a collaborative culture. Long-term customer relationships, a proven track record of performance, and a focus on environmental sustainability and resilience further strengthen its value proposition.
